proposals.evidence: DEDR2598 explicitly gives Gondi hī-/ī-/sī- give. Southern Gondi (Aheri) Grammar, printed p51, example129, has hīm segmented as hī-0 give-IMP_S, visually verified. This directly supports the survey (h)im imperative, including optional h, without postulating an extra lexical component. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR600 gives Gondi un-/unḍānā (past uṭ-/uṭṭ-) drink. Survey unˑudu and untanu retain the un- drinking root with grammatical endings, not a separate lexical subject or auxiliary. The source consonant timing and first-person-style ending are preserved without imposing one dialect’s tense analysis. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
